A.explanation: Air drag opposes motion, so horizontal speed falls below $v$ and upward vertical drag slows the fall, so flight time exceeds $T$.

B.explanation: Horizontal velocity is reduced by drag, but the time cannot stay $T$ because upward drag reduces the vertical acceleration.

C.explanation: Flight time does increase, but horizontal velocity cannot stay $v$ because there is a backward drag force with no forward force to balance it.

D.explanation: This describes motion with no air resistance, where horizontal velocity stays $v$ and fall time is $T$.

hints: Notice the ball starts with horizontal velocity $v$ and zero vertical velocity, with independent horizontal and vertical motions.
Recall drag always opposes the velocity, so think about a backward horizontal component and an upward vertical component while falling.
Connect the upward vertical drag to a smaller net downward force than $mg$, and the backward horizontal drag to continuous horizontal deceleration.
walkthrough: Without air resistance, horizontal velocity stays $v$ because there is no horizontal force, and vertical fall with acceleration $g$ from the tower height gives time $T$.
With air resistance, the drag force acts opposite to the velocity of the ball through the air.
Horizontally, drag has a backward component throughout the flight, so $a_x < 0$ and the horizontal velocity continuously decreases from $v$ to a value less than $v$ at landing.
Vertically, while the ball falls downward, drag has an upward component, so net downward force is $mg - D_y$ and net downward acceleration is less than $g$.
A smaller vertical acceleration means the same vertical height takes longer to fall, so the flight time is more than $T$.
Reduced horizontal velocity combined with increased flight time matches less than $v$ after more than $T$ seconds. This is option A.
